10pub(crate) enum GlyphSpan<'a, T>
11where
12    T: Glyph,
13{
14    Unspanned(&'a [T]),
15    Spanned(&'a [T], &'a str),
16}
17
18impl<T> GlyphSpan<'_, T>
19where
20    T: Glyph,
21{
22    pub(crate) fn glyphs(&self) -> &[T] {
23        match self {
24            GlyphSpan::Unspanned(glyphs) => glyphs,
25            GlyphSpan::Spanned(glyphs, _) => glyphs,
26        }
27    }
28
29    pub(crate) fn actual_text(&self) -> Option<&str> {
30        match self {
31            GlyphSpan::Unspanned(_) => None,
32            GlyphSpan::Spanned(_, text) => Some(text),
33        }
34    }
35}

37/// In PDF, correspondences between glyphs and Unicode codepoints are expressed
38/// via a CMAP. In a CMAP, you can assign a sequence of Unicode codepoints to each
39/// glyph. There are two issues with this approach:
40/// - How to deal with the fact that the same glyph might be assigned two different codepoints
41///   in different contexts (i.e. space and NZWJ).
42/// - How to deal with complex shaping scenarios, where there is not a one-to-one or
43///   one-to-many correspondence between glyphs and codepoints, but instead a many-to-one
44///   or many-to-many mapping.
45///
46/// The answer to this is the `ActualText` feature of PDF, which allows to define some custom
47/// actual text for a number of glyphs, which overrides anything else. Unfortunately, this
48/// is seemingly only supported in Acrobat and Chrome, but it's the only proper way of addressing
49/// this issue.
50///
51/// This is the task of the `TextSpanner`. Given a sequence of glyphs, it segments the
52/// sequence into subruns of glyphs that either do need to be wrapped in an actual text
53/// attribute, or not.
54pub(crate) struct GlyphSpanner<'a, T>
55where
56    T: Glyph,
57{
58    slice: &'a [T],
59    context_color: rgb::Color,
60    reversed: bool,
61    forbid_invalid_codepoints: bool,
62    font_container: Rc<RefCell<FontContainer>>,
63    text: &'a str,
64}
65
66impl<'a, T> GlyphSpanner<'a, T>
67where
68    T: Glyph,
69{
70    pub(crate) fn new(
71        slice: &'a [T],
72        text: &'a str,
73        reversed: bool,
74        forbid_invalid_codepoints: bool,
75        context_color: rgb::Color,
76        font_container: Rc<RefCell<FontContainer>>,
77    ) -> Self {
78        Self { slice, context_color, reversed, forbid_invalid_codepoints, text, font_container }
79    }
80}
81
82impl<'a, T> Iterator for GlyphSpanner<'a, T>
83where
84    T: Glyph,
85{
86    type Item = GlyphSpan<'a, T>;
87
88    #[inline]
89    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
90        fn func<U>(
91            g: &U,
92            context_color: rgb::Color,
93            previous_range: Option<Range<usize>>,
94            forbid_invalid_codepoints: bool,
95            mut font_container: RefMut<FontContainer>,
96            text: &str,
97        ) -> (Range<usize>, bool)
98        where
99            U: Glyph,
100        {
101            let (identifier, pdf_glyph) = font_container.add_glyph(ColoredGlyph::new(g.glyph_id(), context_color));
102            let pdf_font = font_container.get_from_identifier_mut(identifier.clone()).unwrap();
103
104            let range = g.text_range().clone();
105            let text = &text[range.clone()];
106            let codepoints = pdf_font.get_codepoints(pdf_glyph);
107            // Check if the glyph has already been assigned codepoints that don't match the
108            // one we are seeing right now.
109            let incompatible_codepoint = codepoints.is_some_and(|c| c != text);
110
111            // Only set the codepoint if there isn't a previous, different mapping.
112            //
113            // If we could set it, we only want to insert a codepoint if we are not already
114            // building a spanned run (which is the case if the previous range is the same).
115            // If we are building a spanned run, it means that the glyphs are part of the same
116            // cluster, in which case only the first glyph should be assigned the codepoint,
117            // while all other glyphs in the same cluster should not be assigned anything.
118            // Otherwise, when copying text from the PDF, we will get the same codepoint multiple
119            // times in viewers that don't support `ActualText`.
120            //
121            // However, in case we are for example exporting to PDF/UA, every glyph is required
122            // to have a valid codepoint mapping. So in this case, we still add the codepoints
123            // to each glyph in the cluster, this will result in worse copy-pasting in viewers
124            // that don't support `ActualText`.
125            if !incompatible_codepoint && (previous_range != Some(range.clone()) || forbid_invalid_codepoints) && codepoints != Some(text) {
126                pdf_font.set_codepoints(pdf_glyph, text.to_string(), g.location());
127            }
128
129            (range, incompatible_codepoint)
130        }
131
132        let mut use_span = None;
133        let mut count = 1;
134
135        let mut iter = self.slice.iter();
136
137        // Get the range of the first glyph, as well as whether it's
138        // incompatible.
139        let (first_range, first_incompatible) =
140            func(iter.next()?, self.context_color, None, self.forbid_invalid_codepoints, self.font_container.borrow_mut(), self.text);
141
142        let mut prev_range = first_range.clone();
143
144        for next in iter {
145            let (next_range, next_incompatible) =
146                func(next, self.context_color, Some(prev_range.clone()), self.forbid_invalid_codepoints, self.font_container.borrow_mut(), self.text);
147
148            match use_span {
149                // In this case, we just started and we are looking at the first two glyphs.
150                // This decides whether the current run will be spanned, or not.
151                None => {
152                    if prev_range == next_range {
153                        // The two glyphs are in the same range, so we definitely want this run
154                        // to be spanned, and also want to include both glyphs in that run.
155                        use_span = Some(true);
156                    } else {
157                        // Else, whether we use a span depends on whether the first glyph
158                        // is incompatible.
159                        use_span = Some(first_incompatible);
160
161                        // If either the first glyph or the second glyph are incompatible, they
162                        // need to be in separate runs, since they are not part of the same cluster.
163                        if first_incompatible || next_incompatible {
164                            break;
165                        }
166
167                        // If none are incompatible, then `use_span` is false, and we can also
168                        // include the next glyph in that unspanned run.
169                    }
170                }
171                // We are currently building a spanned range, and all glyphs
172                // are part of the same cluster.
173                Some(true) => {
174                    // If the next glyph is not part of the same cluster, terminate the current
175                    // span and don't include the next one.
176                    if prev_range != next_range {
177                        break;
178                    }
179                }
180                // We are currently building an unspanned range, meaning the
181                // glyphs are not part of the same cluster.
182                Some(false) => {
183                    // If the previous and next glyph are part of the same range this means
184                    // that they are part of the same cluster. This means that the previous
185                    // AND the next glyph should be part of the upcoming spanned range, not
186                    // the current one. To exclude the next glyph, we need to do
187                    // `count -= 1` before terminating.
188                    if prev_range == next_range {
189                        count -= 1;
190                        break;
191                    }
192
193                    // If the next one is incompatible, terminate the
194                    // current run, since the next one needs to be spanned.
195                    if next_incompatible {
196                        break;
197                    }
198                }
199            }
200
201            prev_range = next_range;
202            count += 1;
203
204            // PDF 1.7 § 14.8.2.3.3 says that `/ReversedChars` show strings shall not contain
205            // interior space glyphs. Thus, we check whether we have a glyph that is not the first
206            // one and which has a space as its text mapping, and if so, stop after it. That a space
207            // is in the same cluster as another codepoint should be exceedingly rare, so we do a
208            // literal comparison against `" "` instead of a containment check and prefer to
209            // continue otherwise.
210            if self.reversed && count > 1 && &self.text[prev_range.clone()] == " " {
211                break;
212            }
213        }
214
215        // If we only had one glyph to begin with (and never entered the for loop), then
216        // it should be spanned if its codepoint is incompatible.
217        if count == 1 {
218            use_span = Some(first_incompatible);
219        }
220
221        let (head, tail) = self.slice.split_at(count);
222        self.slice = tail;
223
224        let fragment = match use_span.unwrap_or(false) {
225            true => GlyphSpan::Spanned(head, &self.text[first_range]),
226            false => GlyphSpan::Unspanned(head),
227        };
228
229        Some(fragment)
230    }
231}

233pub(crate) struct GlyphGroup<'a, T>
234where
235    T: Glyph,
236{
237    pub(crate) font_identifier: FontIdentifier,
238    pub(crate) glyphs: &'a [T],
239    // This will be stored in normalized form (i.e. at a font size of 1).
240    pub(crate) y_offset: f32,
241    // This will be stored in normalized form (i.e. at a font size of 1).
242    pub(crate) y_advance: f32,
243}
244
245impl<'a, T> GlyphGroup<'a, T>
246where
247    T: Glyph,
248{
249    pub fn from_props(glyphs: &'a [T], props: GlyphProps) -> Self {
250        GlyphGroup { font_identifier: props.font_identifier, glyphs, y_offset: props.y_offset, y_advance: props.y_advance }
251    }
252}
253
254// The GlyphGrouper further segments glyph runs (that already have been segmented
255// by `TextSpanner` into subruns that can be encoded as one consecutive run in PDF.
256// This is necessary because:
257// - The user provides a font for the whole glyph run, but in PDF, the font might
258// have to be switched if the glyph maps to a different Type3 font.
259// - The glyph contains a y_offset/y_advance, which cannot be expressed as an adjustment
260// and requires us to start a new run with a transformation matrix that takes this
261// adjustment into account.
262pub(crate) struct GlyphGrouper<'a, T>
263where
264    T: Glyph,
265{
266    font_container: Rc<RefCell<FontContainer>>,
267    context_color: rgb::Color,
268    slice: &'a [T],
269}
270
271impl<'a, T> GlyphGrouper<'a, T>
272where
273    T: Glyph,
274{
275    pub fn new(font_container: Rc<RefCell<FontContainer>>, context_color: rgb::Color, slice: &'a [T]) -> Self {
276        Self { font_container, context_color, slice }
277    }
278}
279
280impl<'a, T> Iterator for GlyphGrouper<'a, T>
281where
282    T: Glyph,
283{
284    type Item = GlyphGroup<'a, T>;
285
286    #[inline]
287    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
288        // Guarantees: All glyphs in `head` have the font identifier that is given in
289        // `props`, the same size and the same y offset.
290        let (head, tail, props) = {
291            let mut count = 1;
292
293            let mut iter = self.slice.iter();
294            let first = get_glyph_props(iter.next()?, self.context_color, &mut self.font_container.borrow_mut());
295
296            for next in iter {
297                let temp_glyph = get_glyph_props(next, self.context_color, &mut self.font_container.borrow_mut());
298
299                // If either of those is different, we need to start a new subrun.
300                if first.font_identifier != temp_glyph.font_identifier
301                    || first.y_offset != temp_glyph.y_offset
302                    || first.y_advance != 0.0
303                    || temp_glyph.y_advance != 0.0
304                {
305                    break;
306                }
307
308                count += 1;
309            }
310
311            let (head, tail) = self.slice.split_at(count);
312            (head, tail, first)
313        };
314
315        self.slice = tail;
316
317        let glyph_group = GlyphGroup::from_props(head, props);
318
319        Some(glyph_group)
320    }
321}

323pub(crate) struct GlyphProps {
324    font_identifier: FontIdentifier,
325    y_offset: f32,
326    y_advance: f32,
327}
328
329pub(crate) fn get_glyph_props<U>(g: &U, context_color: rgb::Color, font_container: &mut FontContainer) -> GlyphProps
330where
331    U: Glyph,
332{
333    // Safe because we've already added all glyphs in the text spanner.
334    let font_identifier = font_container.font_identifier(ColoredGlyph::new(g.glyph_id(), context_color)).unwrap();
335
336    GlyphProps { font_identifier, y_offset: g.y_offset(1.0), y_advance: g.y_advance(1.0) }
337}
338
339pub fn use_text_spanner(glyphs: &[impl Glyph], text: &str, context_color: rgb::Color, font_container: &mut FontContainer) -> bool {
340    if glyphs.is_empty() {
341        return false;
342    }
343
344    let mut do_text_span = false;
345    // We _might_ need to group glyphs either if they are mapped to different PDF fonts (which
346    // can only happen for Type3 fonts, not CID fonts), or if a glyph has a different y/x offset.
347    // Note that it's of course possible that we always use the same Type3 font, but we need to
348    // be conservative here.
349
350    let mut check_single = |glyph, do_text_span: &mut bool| {
351        // As soon as we know that the glyph run requires a text span, we do not insert any codepoints
352        // anymore, because otherwise we might unnecessarily pollute the cmap with entries that
353        // wouldn't be necessary. The text spanner will then iterate over the all glyphs again
354        // and thus take care of inserting cmap entries for any remaining glyphs we ignore now.
355        // The only reason we keep going and don't early abort is in order to fully
356        // check the `do_glyph_grouping` property.
357        if !*do_text_span {
358            check_text_span_prop(glyph, text, context_color, font_container, do_text_span);
359        }
360    };
361
362    for glyphs in glyphs.windows(2) {
363        let prev = &glyphs[0];
364        let next = &glyphs[1];
365
366        // If two glyphs are part of the same cluster, we definitely need a text span.
367        do_text_span |= prev.text_range() == next.text_range();
368
369        check_single(prev, &mut do_text_span);
370    }
371
372    // Since windows checks groups of two, we need to manually check the last glyph
373    check_single(glyphs.last().unwrap(), &mut do_text_span);
374
375    do_text_span
376}
377
378fn check_text_span_prop(glyph: &impl Glyph, text: &str, context_color: rgb::Color, font_container: &mut FontContainer, do_text_span: &mut bool) {
379    let (identifier, pdf_glyph) = font_container.add_glyph(ColoredGlyph::new(glyph.glyph_id(), context_color));
380    let pdf_font = font_container.get_from_identifier_mut(identifier.clone()).unwrap();
381
382    let range = glyph.text_range().clone();
383    let text = &text[range.clone()];
384    let codepoints = pdf_font.get_codepoints(pdf_glyph);
385
386    if codepoints.is_some_and(|t| t != text) {
387        // If there already exists an entry, then the codepoints are invalid, and we will have to
388        // use a text span.
389        *do_text_span = true;
390    } else if codepoints.is_none() {
391        pdf_font.set_codepoints(pdf_glyph, text.to_string(), glyph.location());
392    }
393}
